contributions.statement: Do not inject an always-on LLM coach/supervisor into the agent loop: on GPT-4.1 it raised turns about 2.5x and files read about 3.4x while lowering judged grounding of conclusions.
contributions.evidence: §4.3 Fig. 12: 24 trajectories, one model, DeepSeek-V3 as coach and judges; grounding median ~0.68 vs 0.85-0.95, scored by LLM judges whose human alignment is weakest on grounding (App. 11 Table 15).

contributions.statement: Tight turn budgets on read-only code-understanding tasks shrink exploration (turns, files, LOC) without a matching collapse in judged answer quality, but stopping calibration gets worse (0.715 to 0.633).
contributions.evidence: §4.1-4.2 Figs. 4-5 and P24 evidence; one trajectory per grid cell, quality judged by LLMs; Python/TS/Rust repos, no change tasks.

contributions.statement: Prompt-condition changes moved agent behaviour far less than switching models (task relevance 0.17-0.87 across models vs 0.61-0.63 across conditions).
contributions.evidence: §4.2.2-4.2.3 Fig. 8, Table 6; single run per cell.

reason: The coach-judge caution and the budget nuance are plausible but rest on 24 runs and LLM-judged quality; the moderate finding (models matter more than prompts) is already known.
